`python3 budget.py 2026-09` now counts only September's transactions, and running it with no argument gives the same all-time totals as before.

I ran it against your data:

| Envelope | No month (unchanged) | `2026-08` | `2026-09` |
|---|---|---|---|
| groceries | 174.60 | 403.05 | 371.55 |
| fuel | 22.85 | 78.10 | 124.75 |
| eating out | 45.75 | 111.50 | 84.25 |
| household | 54.61 | 73.01 | 101.60 |

- **Month format:** it must be exactly `YYYY-MM`. Anything else (`2026-9`, `2026-13`) prints an error and exits with status 2 rather than silently showing all-time totals.
- **Empty months:** a month with no transactions (e.g. `2026-07`) shows every envelope at its full allocation, with no warning.

The change is all in `budget.py`: two small helpers (`parse_month`, `in_month`) plus the argument handling in `main`, and the usage line in the docstring is updated.
